bib.title: CODET: CODE GENERATION WITH GENERATED TESTS

question: How can one pick the correct code solution from many LM samples without human-written tests?
hypothesis: Correct solutions pass more LM-generated tests and agree with more other solutions; incorrect solutions are diverse and rarely agree by chance (RANSAC-like assumptions).
contributions: CodeT: LM-generated test cases plus dual execution agreement for solution selection
Evaluation on five models and four benchmarks, with large pass@1 gains
Analysis of test case quality, quantity and scoring variants

method.summary: Sample N code solutions and M assert-style test cases from the same pretrained LM (zero-shot, with a test-generation instruction appended). Execute every solution on every test, group solutions passing identical test sets into consensus sets, score each set by sqrt(|Sx|)*|Sy| and return a solution from the top-ranked set(s). No training; pure inference-time reranking.
method.task: code generation with solution selection / reranking

datasets.name: HumanEval
datasets.preprocessing: example input-output cases removed from context; avg 7.77 GT tests; n=100 samples

datasets.name: MBPP (sanitized)
datasets.preprocessing: context built like HumanEval; avg 3.1 GT tests; n=100

datasets.name: APPS
datasets.preprocessing: examples removed; header def solution(stdin : str) -> str:; avg 20.99 GT tests; n=50

datasets.name: CodeContests
datasets.preprocessing: same as APPS; avg 203.7 GT tests; n=1000

inference.decoding: top-p sampling; baseline pass@1 uses greedy (temperature 0)
inference.samples: HumanEval/MBPP 100 code samples; APPS 50; CodeContests 1000; test cases: 100 samples per problem (HumanEval, MBPP), 50 (APPS, CodeContests), first 5 valid asserts per sample (Limit 5)
inference.prompting: zero-shot; test generation appends instruction: pass placeholder, comment 'check the correctness of [entry point]', and 'assert'

parameters.consensus_score: f(S)=sqrt(|Sx|)*|Sy| (sqrt on solution count, Appendix A); paper main text defines f=|Sx||Sy|
parameters.valid_test: starts with assert and contains entry point name
parameters.top_k: k consensus sets, one solution from each; cycles if fewer than k sets
parameters.RANSAC_iterations: naive version enumerates all pairs; no iteration count given

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: percent of problems where any of k selected solutions passes all ground-truth tests; baseline uses unbiased estimator (Chen 2021) with k random from n; CodeT selects k via consensus sets

metrics.name: test case accuracy / toxicity rate / coverage
metrics.definition: accuracy: canonical solution passes the test; toxic: some generated solution passes but canonical fails; statement and branch coverage via Coverage.py

baselines: AlphaCode-C (replication of Li et al. 2022b clustering)
eval.protocol: single run, no seeds or significance tests reported

evidence.quote: we use the square root of |Sx| to reduce the impact caused by code solutions

limits: Only works for executable code and adds test-generation compute cost (Conclusion).
Gains small on hard problems (APPS competition, CodeContests) because generated tests are low quality; one-shot CodeT Filter can be slightly worse than baseline on CodeContests.

Relies on assumption that incorrect solutions rarely agree; fails with ambiguous specs, uncovered corner cases, or misunderstood problems (53/164 HumanEval cases with cushman-001 had a correct solution outside top-1).
Example I/O removed from prompts, so numbers differ from original HumanEval; leaving them in leaks real tests into CodeT (Appendix B).
Single run, no variance or significance reported; compute cost of 100 code plus 100 test samples per problem not quantified.
Codex models code-cushman/davinci are deprecated; not reproducible via API now.
